subject: count data as a covariate within occuRN

messages.author: ed1c65b7e0d2b3fe
messages.subject: count data as a covariate within occuRN
parts:
Hello everyone,

I have a question regarding the use of count data as a covariate
within occuRN. I have sites with both single and multiple individual
responses. Rather than restricting each site to present or absent
(which is what occuRN does automatically), I wanted to account for
variation in the number of individuals responding at each site by
including them as a covariate. (i.e., Am I more likely to detect an
individual where many respond vs. where 1 responds).

Would it be appropriate if I used the count data (the sum of the
number of individuals responding over all encounter histories at each
site) as a covariate of detection or would I be confounding detection
by using observed results.

Thank you in advance,

Tyler Petroelje

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] count data as a covariate within occuRN
parts:
Dear Tyler,

if you have counts, it is better to directly model abundance using pcount(). If you want to estimate occupancy probability you can get it as 1 minus the probability to obtain a zero count under the Poisson distribution fitted to the data. See the useful paper by Dorazio (Ecology, 2007) for the relationships among three hierarchical models that can be used for inference about distributions.

Kind regards -- Marc

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Re: count data as a covariate within occuRN
parts:
Dear Tyler,

the N-mixture model fitted with pcount is the natural counterpart to the site-occupancy model when you have counts with imperfect detection, instead of detection/nondetection observations with imperfect detection. Counts contain more information about the underlying abundance distribution than detection/nondetection observations, therefore it's best not to throw away info by reducing them to detection/nondetections (a.k.a. "presence/absence" data).

Kind regards -- Marc

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: count data as a covariate within occuRN
parts:
Tyler,

To add to Marc's comments, the references which are cited in ?pcount
and also the article at http://www.jstatsoft.org/v43/i10/ would help
explain how the N-mixture model combines a detection model with a
latent count abundance model. Basically, there's a latent Poisson
model for abundance and then a binomial model for detection
conditional on abundance.

Hope that helps,
Ian

Richard

parts:
Hi Tyler,

it appears to me from the sample data that you don't have enough low counts with so many zeroes. Instead there are lots of 2's, 4's and 5's. I assume that coyotes don't travel singly but in pairs or groups and this non-independence could also cause problems. Basically, the binomial mixture model assumes independence of individual detections.

Regards -- Marc
